sources.news_title: Dem Candidate Abdul El-Sayed Deletes Podcast Where He Called to Scrap July 4th Fireworks and the Second Amendment.
sources.text:
Michigan Democrat Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed is under fire for past remarks, including criticism of July 4 traditions and calls to abolish Americans’ Second Amendment right to bear arms.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED:Michigan Democrat Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed criticized July 4 fireworks and proposed abolishing Americans’ right to bear arms in a podcast episode.
📺 DETAIL: In a podcast episode from July 2024 that has since been made private, El-Sayed criticized July 4 fireworks.“Fireworks suck,” declared El-Sayed in a sub-section titled “Fireworks just aren’t worth it:hear us out.” Specifically, he took aim at the environmental impact of July 4 fireworks, among other things. El-Sayed also suggested removing the right to bear armsin favor of aright to healthcare. “What if we tweaked the Constitution, amended the amendment, and instead of the right to bear arms, we change it to the right to have health care?” said El-Sayed. He also dismissed the southern border as a priority, claiming that Republicans “love to flog” the issue and suggesting that illegal immigration was not an important issueto voters. This follows the uncovering of a recording of El-Sayed calling to“defund the police”in 2020. El-Sayed’s criticism of July 4 traditions was endorsed by The Marguerite Casey Foundation,a progressive grantmaking organization. El-Sayed’s campaign claims these remarks do not reflect his current views, although over 100 videos have been removed from his platforms since his Senate run began.
🎯 IMPACT: El-Sayed’s past remarks could become a focal pointin the state’s general election. As Michigan is a swing state, many voters are likely to find El-Sayed’s extreme-left views off-putting. Republicans have sought to leverage El-Sayed’s past comments as a means to mobilize moderate voters against him. His nomination demonstrates the ongoing shift to the leftwithin the Democrat Party and the mainstreaming ofanti-American sentiment.
📺 FLASHBACK: El-Sayed’s comments reflect a similar sentiment expressed by Francesca Hong,a Democrat state representative in Wisconsin and member of the far-left Democratic Socialists of America.Hong called to “Cancel Thanksgiving”and said she felt “attacked” by a Christmas-themed computer background display in previous posts on X (formerly Twitter).
BREAKING: Abdul El-Sayed DELTED a 2024 podcast where he said "July 4th Fireworks Suck"
Major U.S. airlines are obstructing federal immigration enforcement efforts, raising concerns over national security as the 25th anniversary of 9/11 approaches.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: Federal immigration enforcement at U.S. airports has intensified ahead of the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, prompting disputes between Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and several major airlines over how arrests should be conducted.
📺 DETAIL: ICE reportedly averaged nearly three dozen airport arrests per day in July, including foreign nationals who had overstayed visas or received final deportation orders. Airlines such as Southwestand JetBluehave challenged aspects of the enforcement operations, with employees in some cases restricting agents’ access to boarding areas and passenger information. During a July 25 incident in Dallas, Southwest personnel reportedly refused to allow ICE agents onto a departing aircraft without a judicial warrant, while agents were using an administrative warrant issued by ICE. The renewed debate over visa enforcement has drawn attention to the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, as the 9/11 Commission found that as many as five of the 19 hijackers had overstayed their visas.
🎯 IMPACT: The standoff between airlines and federal authorities underscores a critical tension in enforcing immigration laws and ensuring nationalsecurity. With the anniversary of 9/11 approaching, the airlines’ refusal to cooperate raises concerns about vulnerabilities in the aviation sector, particularly as past terrorist plots have exploited visa overstays.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “Airlines have had constructive discussions with ICE and TSA to ensure if law-enforcement activity occurs at an airport, there are proper proceduresand protocols in place to prioritize the safety and security of all involved,” claimed a spokesman for Airlines for America.

Two former Chinese military officers have been detained in South Korea, accused of spying near critical U.S. military installations.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED:South Koreanauthorities have arrested two former Chinese military officersaccused of spying on or around major U.S. military installations.
📍 WHEN & WHERE: The incidents occurred near Gunsan Air Baseand Camp Humphreys, two critical U.S. military installations located south of Seoul, South Korea. Gunsan is home to the U.S. 8th Fighter Wing, while Camp Humphreys is the largest U.S. military base outside continental America.
📺 DETAIL: One suspect, a Chinese national in his sixties, allegedly monitored air traffic control communications near Kunsan Air Base during multiple visits to South Korea that coincided with major U.S.-South Korean military exercises. The second suspect, a 45-year-old Chinese-Korean national who operated a military surplus store near Camp Humphreys in Pyeongtaek, is accused of recruiting a South Korean employee at the base to obtain classified information about joint military exercises. Police said the alleged espionage activities involving the second suspect began in 2021, though authorities have not released the suspects’ names or arrest details. The men could face charges under South Korea’s Communications Secrets Protection Act and Military Base Protection Act, while an alleged violation of the Benefiting the Enemy Act could carry a life sentence.
🎯 IMPACT: The arrests come at a diplomatically sensitive moment, as Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi is set to visit South Korea. The case underscores growing concerns over China’s espionage activities in the region, particularly against U.S. bases, which play a critical role in monitoring the strategic Yellow Sea and countering potential threats from China’s PLA.
📺 FLASHBACK: Former South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol previously cited Chinese espionage as a justification for martial law in 2024, a move that led to his impeachment. His successor, Lee Jae-myung, has sought closer ties with Beijing while maintaining defense cooperation with the U.S.

A federal judge ruled that Minnesota’s claims against the Trump administration’s executive order declaring there are only two sexes lacked a sufficient legal basis.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: A federal judge has largely rejected Minnesota’s legal challenge to President Donald J. Trump’s policies defining sex as male or female, ruling that the state had not demonstrated an immediate legal injury from the administration’s actions.
📺 DETAIL: Minnesota had argued that the Trump administration violated the Administrative Procedure Act and infringed on state authority, but the judge found those claims unpersuasive. Trump’s January 2025 executive order, titled “Defending Women From Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government,” directed federal agencies to recognize only two sexes, male and female, and to base federal policy on biological sex. The order formed part of the Trump administration’s broader effort to restrict transgender participation in women’s sports and alter federal policies concerning gender identity, prompting lawsuits from Democrat-led states, leftist advocacy groups, and other organizations. Some portions of Trump’s broader gender-related agenda have faced judicial setbacks, including rulings challenging federal restrictions tied to gender ideology. Other challenges remain pending or have been dismissed.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “Minnesota will not face legal consequences unless and until a hearing is held in which the relevant agency finds that Minnesota is not in compliance with Title IX, or a court finds, in a civil enforcement action, that Minnesota is not in compliance with Title IX.” – Judge Eric Tostrud
🎯 IMPACT: The ruling underscores the difficulty states face in challenging the Trump administration’s federal policies without clear evidence of legal violations. It also reinforces the Trump administration’s efforts to maintain its policies on gender and biological sex, particularly in areas like women’s sports.

Far-left activists in Clacton-on-Sea, England, were caught on CCTV taking down boards showing support for Nigel Farage, leader of the Reform UK party, as he prepares to fight a parliamentary by-election (special election) on Thursday.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: Far-left activists have been caught taking down signs showing support for Reform UK party Nigel Faragein the Clacton-on-Sea constituency (electoral district) in England.
📺 DETAIL:Revealed exclusively by The National Pulse on Tuesday, the CCTV footage shows far-left activists taking down signs expressing support for Farage ahead of the Clacton-on-Sea by-election (special election) on Thursday. The activists were caught in the act early Friday morning. One of the activists can be heard saying, “I’m only taking down Reform signs.”
💬 KEY QUOTE: “Far left activists have been caught ripping down Reform UK/Nigel Farage boards in Clacton-on-Sea in the dead of night. They were caught on CCTV early Friday morning. Local police have been notified and the incident underscores the dirty tricks the left get up to in places they know they can’t win.” – Raheem Kassam, Editor-in-Chief of The National Pulse, on X (formerly Twitter).
🎯 IMPACT: Local police have been notified of the incident. The Clacton-on-Sea by-election was triggered after Nigel Farage, then-Member of Parliament (MP) for Clacton, resigned to protest to a weaponized parliamentary probe against him. After announcing his resignation, Farage put his name forward for the resulting by-election, declaring that the people of Clacton, not the political establishment, should determine whether he is fit to represent the area. As Farage is on course to win the by-election by a comfortable margin, this story shows how the establishment-backed oppositionhas resorted to dirty tactics in a last-ditch attempt to hurt the Reform leader.
📺 FLASHBACK: The National Pulse previously revealed that Afghan migrants were distributing anti-Nigel Farage material around the Clacton-on-Sea constituency. “On the campaign trail today in Clacton, we encountered a group of recent Afghan migrants delivering leaflets on behalf of Dale Vince’s anti-Reform Babelfish newspaper. Vince, a Labour and Green Party donor, recently announced he intended to spend money campaigning against Farage, though hasn’t registered as a campaigner in the constituency. Not only is this legally murky, but ethically an obviously huge issue,” noted Raheem Kassam, Editor-in-Chief of The National Pulse.

A new poll shows former Vice President Kamala Harris leading California Governor Gavin Newsom and New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez among Democrat primaryvoters, suggesting the defeated 2024 presidential candidate is still seen as viable by the party grassroots.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: Former Vice President Kamala Harris has topped a poll for the 2028 Democrat presidential primary.
📺 DETAIL: In a new poll from Rasmussen Reports, former Vice President Harris secured 37 percent, significantly outpacing Governor of California Gavin Newsom at14 percent and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at nine percent. Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) also polled at nine percent, while former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg secured ten percent. The poll revealed that Harris’s strongest support exists among black voters. The poll also showed that 53 percent of voters under 40 said they favored Harris, with support for the failed 2024 candidate dropping significantlywith voters over 65. The poll was carried out between August 2 and August 4, 2026, on 504 likely Democrat primary voters.
🎯 IMPACT: Harris’s early lead suggests she remains a dominant figureamong Democrats and Democrat-aligned voters, despite losing to President Donald J. Trump in the 2024 presidential election. Harris lost both the Electoral Collegeand the popular vote.While Harris has topped this poll, other surveys show the former Vice President polling in the single digits.The new poll could suggest that Democrat voters view Harris as a unifying figure amid the party’s descent into civil war over whether to embrace the far-left politicsof the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).
💬 KEY QUOTE: “It is interesting that AOC has fallen, given the rising star of democratic socialism in Democratic primaries. Maybe there is some buyer’s remorsethat’s being reflected in that poll. It’s still very early, and my hunch remains that Kamala Harris’s support is soft (although she has a core of staunch supporters). I would expect to see some more formal or more serious declarations of interest after the mid-terms.” – Professor Grant Davis Reeher.
📺 FLASHBACK: Back in July, it was reported that Rep. Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) had topped a New Hampshire Democrat primary poll, leading former Transportation Secretary Buttigieg by one percent. Harris polled at five percent.

Robert Gilman, a U.S. military veteran detained in Russia since 2022, has been freed and is now receiving medical care in Texas.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: Robert Gilman, a 32-year-old American military veteran, has been released from Russian custody after spending over four years in prison under reportedly abusive conditions. He is now in Texas receiving medical and psychological treatment, according to advocacy group Global Reach.
📺 DETAIL: Gilman was sentenced in 2022 for allegedly assaulting a police officer and later faced additional charges relating to alleged attacks on investigators, prison inspectors, and guards, extending his prison term to ten years. Reports claim he endured forced exercise, psychotropic drug administration, and harassment, with Russian authorities allegedly pressuring him to fight in Ukraine. He was reportedly in a “dissociative stupor”before being transferred to a civilian hospital.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “I am so grateful to President Trump for saving my brother’s life. There is no other reason that Robert is alive today other than that President Trump heard about the case and took action.” – Lexie Hudson, Gilman’s sister
🎯 IMPACT: Gilman’s release highlights ongoing issues with American citizens detained abroad, with at least eight Americans still in Russian custody.
📺 FLASHBACK: In recent years, U.S.-Russia prisoner exchanges have brought attention to the plight of Americans detained in Russia, including high-profile cases involving athletes and journalists.
Today, after more than four years of detention in Russia, Robert Gilman is on his way home to be reunited with his family. Mr. Gilman joins over 100 Americans whom President Trump has freed during his second term in office.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has outlined a new plan to address critical overcrowding in prisons, which includes placing male criminals in women’s prisons.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham proposed putting male inmates in female prisons on Tuesday, to ease Britain’s prison overcrowding crisis.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “It will be based on a range of options including the three strands of further work I asked him to initiate last week: increasing the rate of removal of foreign national offenders from the prison estate to their country of origin; finding an early resolution to the long-running injustice of IPP [Imprisonment for Public Protection] sentences, which could allow for the release of lower-risk prisoners; and making greater use of the entire prison estate including using the female estate for male offenders.” – Prime Minister Andy Burnham
📺 DETAIL:The proposal comes as the Prime Minister faces pressure to exclude Police Constable (PC) Andrew Harper’s killers from the government’s early release scheme. The scheme is designed to reduce overcrowding by allowing inmates who have served just 40 percent of their sentence to request early release. The scheme includes those convicted of manslaughter, such as the killers of PC Harper, who was dragged to death behind a car after responding to a burglary. “I understand the depth of public concern about the potential early release of those involved with the killing of PC Andrew Harper– and I share it,” said Prime Minister Burnham, who confirmed that his plans to reduce overcrowding include “making greater use of the entire prison estate including using the female estate for male offenders.“
🎯 IMPACT: As the British prison system as a whole is operating at 99 percent capacity, the crisis has become acute, although critics of the Labour Party government believe it should be securing additional spaces, as it does with illegal migrant accommodation, rather than releasing criminals early. The introduction of male inmates into female prisons, which are also nearing maximum capacity, has the potential to spark safety concerns.
📺 FLASHBACK: Earlier this month, the Police Federation, an organization representing rank-and-file police officers, threatened to take the British government to courtif PC Harper’s killers were released early.

Two police officers were injured in Toulouse, France, after a man shouting “Allahu Akbar” attacked them with multiple knives during a patrol.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: A man was subdued after shouting “Allahu Akbar” and attacked two police officers, one of whom was female, in France.
📺 DETAIL: On Monday,a manattacked two police officers with a knife in the Wilson district of Toulouse, France. The officers were on patrol when a man slashed one of the officers in the throatwith a knife. The female officer was also stabbed three times. The attacker shouted “Allahu Akbar” during the incident, according to local police reports. The attacker pulled out two additional knives after dropping his first, but was subsequently restrained after being subdued by police with telescopic batons. The officer who was slashed in the neck required stitches, while the female officer avoided serious injury due to her bulletproof vest.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “[The officers came within] a hair’s breadth of the worst,” said Emilion Esnault, a French local politician, describing the attack.
🎯 IMPACT:An investigation into the attack is ongoing.Local police have also been ordered to remain on high alert until further notice. The fact that the attacker shouted “Allahu Akbar”suggests an Islamist motive. This represents a recurring problem in France, which has experienced multiple Islamist attacks this year. Back in July, a man claimed “it is Allah who ordered me” after stabbing three women in Paris. The three women, one of whom was pregnant, sustained non-lethal injuries. Such attacks are likely to drive support for parties offering a tough law and order stance, measures to bolster national security, immigration restrictions, and anti-Islamist policies, particularly Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN). This is far from solely a French problem, however, as other European countries have suffered similar attacks throughout the year. Also in July, Berlin Pride in Germany was hit by an Islamist attack that left one dead and at least 29 injured. The attacker was known for a “high volume of criminal offenses, radicalization, and affiliation with the Islamist scene,“ according to German officials.

Federal agencies are proposing significant changes to visa programs, aiming to protect American workers and address growing public concern over the displacement of local professionals by foreign labor.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: The Department of Homeland Security and Department of Labor have unveiled draft regulations that would tighten visa programs, including H-1B and F-1 student visas, to prioritize American workers. Proposed changes include higher corporate fees, shorter grace periods for fired foreign workers, and stricter oversight of third-party staffing firms.
📺 DETAIL: The proposed rules also seek to modernize the PERM labor certification process, ensuring American workers are given priority in hiring and addressing layoffs more effectively. Critics of the visa programs argue that they depress wages, displace American workers, and foster job monopolies within certain ethnic networks. Public opposition to these programs has grown in recent years, with unemployment and underemployment rates for U.S. college graduates remaining high, including 26 percent for computer science graduates.
🎯 IMPACT: If implemented, the reforms could significantly reduce reliance on foreign labor, encourage companies to invest in American talent, and potentially sway voters ahead of the midterm elections. However, big business, including lobbying groups like FWD.us, is expected to push back against these measures, given the rewards it reaps from undercutting American workers by importing foreign workers.
📈 DATA: According to the New York Federal Reserve Bank, the combined unemployment and underemployment rate for recent U.S. college graduates is approximately 40 percent, highlighting the need for increased job opportunities for American graduates and professionals.
📺 FLASHBACK: The 60-day grace period for fired foreign workers was introduced in 2017 under the Obama-Biden administration, enabling many visa holders to remain in the U.S. and switch jobs, often to the detriment of American workers.
H-1B is a temporary nonimmigrant visa. If the entire justification for the program is that a foreign worker is admitted only because an American supposedly cannot be found to fill the job, why should that worker get 60 days to remain in the country after being laid off?

A Staten Island court has paused New York City’s new tax on high-value second homes, citing legal challenges from affected homeowners.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED:Staten Island Supreme Court Justice Wayne Ozzi temporarily blocked New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s so-called pied-à-terre tax targeting second homes valued at $5 million or more. The judge’s order halts implementation of the tax until at least August 31, when a court hearing is scheduled, as legal challenges from homeowners proceed.
📺 DETAIL: The city had published a list of properties subject to the tax, but homeowners argued that the rollout was riddled with errors, causing “mass confusion.” Notices were sent to some homeowners incorrectly, and others were threatened that they would face the tax unless they filed for exemptions. The lawsuit claims the city disregarded state data in its assessments. The city must now remove the online list of targeted homes as part of the court’s ruling.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “We disagree with today’s ruling, but we are confident in both the pied-à-terre surcharge and the City’s ability to implement it fairly and effectively.” – Matt Rauschenbach, spokesman for Mayor Zohran Mamdani
🎯 IMPACT: The ruling delays the tax’s implementation and forces the city to reassess its approach amid legal scrutiny. Homeowners argue the tax rollout was unjust and poorly executed, while city officials maintain it is a fair way to generate revenue from wealthy property owners. Mamdani plans to appeal the ruling and proceed with the tax’s implementation.
📺 FLASHBACK: The pied-à-terre tax—a pied-à-terre being an apartment, condominium, or small house in a city lived in part-time—was introduced as part of a broader effort by socialist Mayor Mamdani to redistribute wealth, particularly from white people, and fund city services, which are losing funding as wealthier residents flee New York.

sources.news_title: El-Sayed Faces Questions Over Removed Campaign Videos
sources.text:
Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate Abdul El-Sayed speaks during a Democratic unity rally in Detroit, Michigan, U.S., August 7, 2026. REUTERS/Rebecca Cook TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY
(Detroit, MI) – Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed is facing new questions over more than 100 YouTube videos that were reportedly removed before he launched his campaign.
Transcripts from videos recorded between 2022 and 2024 reportedly include past comments about the Second Amendment, July 4 fireworks and border policy. El-Sayed’s campaign says those comments do not reflect his current beliefs.
The dispute gives Republicans another line of attack in a race expected to help decide control of the Senate. El-Sayed is running as a progressive Democrat and is expected to face Republican Mike Rogers in November.
Campaigns often try to clean up old material before a statewide race, but removing a large archive can invite fresh scrutiny. El-Sayed will likely be pressed to explain which views changed, when they changed and how voters should judge the record.

sources.news_title: Abdul El-Sayed PURGED more than 100 YouTube videos expressing FRINGE beliefs — and they have resurfaced
sources.text:
Sarah Rice/Getty Images (L); Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto/Getty Images (R) 
    
© 2026 Blaze Media LLC. All rights reserved.
Abdul El-Sayed PURGED more than 100 YouTube videos expressing FRINGE beliefs — and they have resurfaced
August 11, 2026
The campaign says the videos no longer 'reflect his beliefs,' despite the latest ones being only 2 years old.
A CNN investigation has found that the Democratic candidate for the U.S. Senate in Michigan has apparently removed more than a hundred YouTube videos expressing his far-left beliefs.
Abdul El-Sayed narrowly won the Democratic nomination from an establishment candidate last Tuesday, leading many to seize upon the contest as further evidence of fringe extremists taking over the party.
Another video no longer accessible to the public had the Democrat calling for the end of the 2nd Amendment guaranteeing gun rights.
Before he ran for the nomination, El-Sayed removed public access to more than 100 videos on his YouTube account, according to the CNN KFILE report.
In one removed video, El-Sayed blasted the Republican Party for focusing on illegal border crossings and claimed illegal immigration should not be a top concern for voters.
Another video no longer accessible to the public had the Democrat calling for the end of the Second Amendment guaranteeing gun rights and instead offered that there should be a constitutional right to health care.
"What if we tweaked the Constitution, amended the amendment, and instead of the 'right to bear arms,' we change it to the right to have health care?" said El-Sayed in the removed video.
One removed video from July 2024 featured El-Sayed arguing that Americans should stop celebrating the Fourth of July with fireworks. He cited the environmental damage and the risk they allegedly pose to veterans with PTSD as well as pets and children.
He also expressed support for "feminist prison abolition" while reading an ad for the show.
El-Sayed's campaign responded to the CNN report in a statement downplaying the video removals.
"Abdul is the former captain of his high school football team, loves Michigan football on Saturdays, and celebrates the Fourth of July with fireworks like the next Michigander," the statement read. "Cherry-picked comments from old podcasts don’t reflect his beliefs today."
Although the campaign said El-Sayed had changed his beliefs since posting the videos, the most recently removed videos were just two years old.
RELATED: 'He's full of s**t': Trump RIPS INTO Abdul El-Sayed after his narrow victory
The campaign claimed he respected the Second Amendment and pointed to recent messages he posted telling Americans to enjoy fireworks on the Fourth of July.
CNN said it had reviewed transcripts of the videos that had been archived before they were removed.
El-Sayed is aiming to defeat Republican candidate Mike Rogers, helping to determine whether Democrats are able to seize control of the Senate in the midterm elections.
The RealClearPolling average currently has Rogers winning with a very slim lead of 44.3% to El-Sayed at 44.0%

Michigan Dem Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed scrubbed past videos of him saying ‘fireworks suck,’ opposing 2nd Amendment
See more of our coverage in your search results.
Add The New York Post on Google
WASHINGTON — Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed scrubbed videos from his YouTube channel in which he claimed that Fourth of July “fireworks suck,” questioned whether American football was “ethical” and floated the elimination of the Second Amendment right to bear arms.
At least 100 of El-Sayed’s videos were made private ahead of his primary win last week, though several had already been archived, CNN’s KFile first reported.

A July 10, 2024, clip showed El-Sayed discussing “alternative ways of celebrating” America’s independence “that might be just as fun and are definitely less destructive,” The video featured time-stamped segments called, “Fireworks just aren’t worth it: hear us out,” and “Fireworks can trigger PTSD in veterans.”

In a third clip, the Democrat suggested replacing the Constitution’s Second Amendment right to bear arms with a right to health care.
El-Sayed was also recorded accusing Republicans of using border security as an issue that they “love to flog” while arguing that it “doesn’t even make the top five among issues that people in the United States actually care about that affect their lives.”
“Abdul is the former captain of his high school football team, loves Michigan football on Saturdays, and celebrates the Fourth of July with fireworks like the next Michigander,” a campaign rep told CNN. “Cherry-picked comments from old podcasts don’t reflect his beliefs today.”
The campaign also pointed to past posts in which El-Sayed celebrated July 4th.
“Happy Fourth of July, Michigan! Enjoy the fireworks as we commit ourselves to building a country where all of us can thrive,” he posted on X last year.

sources.news_title: Abdul El-Sayed Has a Michigan Problem – Jeffrey Lord
sources.text:
Abdul El-Sayed would like to be the next senator from Michigan. That means, among other things, asking Michigan voters to believe the man he is today matters more than the things he said a few years ago.
That may be a harder sell than he expected.
Old videos and podcasts have resurfaced in which El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee, took aim at some fairly familiar pieces of American life: Fourth of July fireworks, the Second Amendment, the southern border and even football.
None of these comments, taken alone, is likely to decide a Senate race. Taken together, though, they begin to form a picture.
In a July 2024 video, El-Sayed urged Americans to rethink the use of fireworks on Independence Day. He cited pollution, injuries, frightened animals and the effect loud explosions can have on veterans suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder.
The segment was titled, “Fireworks just aren’t worth it.”
There is a practical argument there. But politics is rarely only about the practical argument.
The Fourth of July is not simply a municipal noise-management problem. It is one of those old American rituals — loud, imperfect, slightly ridiculous and deeply loved — that politicians tamper with at some risk.
Then there is the Second Amendment.
After the 2023 school shooting in Nashville, El-Sayed wondered aloud whether the Constitution itself ought to be rewritten.
“What if we tweaked the Constitution, amended the amendment, and instead of the right to bear arms, we change it to the right to have health care?” he asked.
It is the kind of line that plays differently in a progressive podcast than it does in a statewide Michigan election.
The same is true of immigration.
In a 2022 video, El-Sayed said Republicans “love to flog” the southern border and argued the issue did not even rank among the five most important concerns affecting Americans’ lives.
Republicans will surely remind voters of that one.
And then there is football, which in Michigan is not merely a sport so much as a civic language.
In a 2023 podcast, El-Sayed described football as connected to a “particularly masculine and oftentimes toxically masculine culture” and wondered whether there could be a version of the game that was truly “ethical” and “safe.”
Later, he went further, saying episodes in American history including the destruction of Native Americans and the trans-Atlantic slave trade were “echoed in the ethos of football.”
This is an unusual thing to say anywhere. It is an especially unusual thing to say if you later plan to ask Michigan voters to send you to the United States Senate.
El-Sayed’s campaign now says these remarks are being cherry-picked and do not reflect his current beliefs.
“Abdul is the former captain of his high school football team, loves Michigan football on Saturdays, and celebrates the Fourth of July with fireworks like the next Michigander,” his campaign said.
Fair enough.
People change. Politicians change. Sometimes they even say plainly that they were wrong.
But that creates the question El-Sayed will probably have to answer between now and November: Which beliefs changed, and why?
He narrowly defeated the more moderate Rep. Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary and now faces Republican Mike Rogers in a race expected to be highly competitive.
Rogers’ campaign has already begun portraying El-Sayed as too far left for Michigan.
The old clips make that argument easier because they touch something larger than policy. They touch temperament.
Voters often forgive an unpopular position. What they are less certain about is a worldview — particularly one that seems to look at ordinary American traditions and find, first, something suspect.
Fireworks. Guns. Football. The border.
El-Sayed’s problem may not be any one old quote.
It may be the accumulation.

sources.news_title: ‘Fireworks suck’: Removed El-Sayed videos urged getting rid of the 4th of July tradition, raised replacing 2nd Amendment
sources.text:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed once asked his YouTube viewers whether Americans could “PLEASE” find another way to celebrate the Fourth of July, in a video promising four reasons “why fireworks suck.”
The since-removed video from July 2024 included a chapter titled “Fireworks just aren’t worth it: hear us out” and cited Detroit’s post-fireworks air quality, the chemicals used in fireworks, their potential to trigger PTSD in veterans, and the risks they pose to children and pets.
The video is one of several examples of El-Sayed removing past online content as he seeks elected office. As CNN’s KFile previously reported, he also deleted social media posts supporting the “defund the police” movement.
In other since-removed clips, El-Sayed argued that the southern border was not among Americans’ five biggest concerns and lambasted Republicans for focusing on it. In another he floated replacing the Second Amendment’s right to bear arms with a constitutional right to health care.
Not all of El-Sayed’s commentary has disappeared: In one episode that remains online, he questioned whether football could be “ethical” or “safe” and linked the sport’s “ethos” to narratives used to justify slavery and westward expansion.
El-Sayed’s narrow victory last Tuesday over moderate Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens set up a general-election showdown with Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers in a high-stakes race that will help determine control of the US Senate.
The YouTube videos, at least 100 of which appear to have been made private, are another example of how El-Sayed’s years as a prolific podcaster, commentator and social-media user have left behind an extensive record — some of it subsequently deleted — that Republicans could use to portray him as both ideologically left-wing and culturally out of step with swing-state voters.
El-Sayed’s campaign said the old clips do not reflect his current views: “Abdul is the former captain of his high school football team, loves Michigan football on Saturdays, and celebrates the Fourth of July with fireworks like the next Michigander. Cherry-picked comments from old podcasts don’t reflect his beliefs today.”
The campaign pointed CNN to a 2025 social media post in which El-Sayed told followers to enjoy the Fourth of July fireworks. It also said he has long argued for immigration reform that keeps the southern border safe and secure and has criticized ICE’s recent actions under the Trump administration. On guns, the campaign said El-Sayed respects the Second Amendment while supporting policies aimed at keeping guns out of the hands of criminals.
Many of the removed videos on YouTube, where El-Sayed at the time had more than 17,000 subscribers, are not publicly available anymore, but CNN reviewed transcripts archived before the videos were made private.
El-Sayed’s fireworks video was briefly interrupted by a message noting that it was sponsored in part by the Marguerite Casey Foundation. In reading ads for the foundation on his “America Dissected” podcast, he highlighted what he called its “cutting-edge areas of scholarship,” including “feminist prison abolition.”
Prison abolition is a movement that seeks to reduce and ultimately replace prisons, jails, and other punitive systems with approaches intended to address the social conditions linked to harm, including investments in housing, healthcare, education, community-based safety, and restorative or transformative justice. Feminist prison abolitionists argue that incarceration and policing can fail to prevent gender-based violence and may disproportionately harm women and marginalized communities.
The removals were not limited to videos containing potentially damaging political remarks. Lighter material — including a video about plastics and testicles — was also taken down, as was a November 2024 video in which El-Sayed passionately urged viewers to vote for Kamala Harris.
El-Sayed’s past support for the “defund the police” movement has already drawn scrutiny. In 2020 interviews, he said “we do need to defund the police” and described that approach as investing less in policing and more in schools, social services and anti-poverty programs. He has since insisted that he never called for defunding and said his old comments made in deleted tweets uncovered by CNN were taken out of context.
But his remarks on policing represent only one part of a far larger archive.
In a non-deleted episode of his podcast from February 2023, El-Sayed questioned whether any version of football could be “ethical” or “safe” and said narratives that had justified slavery, westward expansion and other forms of oppression were “echoed in the ethos of football.”
In another since-removed video from September 2022, El-Sayed dismissed the southern border as an issue Republicans “love to flog,” saying it “doesn’t even make the top five among issues that people in the United States actually care about that affect their lives.”
He later said Republican voters had been told to care more about the border than inflation, gas prices and pandemics. El-Sayed slammed southern governors like Texas Gov. Greg Abbott and Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis who had flown or bussed migrants to other states, comparing it to his own parents who came to the United States as immigrants.
“It’s crazy to me that the party that says that they’re the party of family values can’t understand when people will make decisions for their families — because that’s exactly what these migrants are doing,” El-Sayed said.
In another since-removed video from April 2023, El-Sayed floated replacing the Second Amendment’s right to bear arms with a constitutional right to health care.
Speaking after a school shooting in Tennessee and as millions of Americans faced losing Medicaid coverage, he asked: “What if we tweaked the Constitution, amended the amendment, and instead of the right to bear arms, we change it to the right to have health care?”
El-Sayed argued that the change would result in “fewer people dying by gun and more people living because they have health care.”
